diagnostics.message:
[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run1]
`google_bigquery_routine.default` builds routine bodies from opaque strings in `var.routines`, so nothing orders it after `google_bigquery_table.default`. SQL routines (scalar and table-valued functions) are validated against the objects their `definition_body` references, so a routine querying a table created by this same module can fail at create time. The module already encodes exactly this constraint for `google_bigquery_table.views` and `google_bigquery_table.materialized_view` via `depends_on = [google_bigquery_table.default]`; routines need the same ordering (bare `depends_on`, since the body is a user-supplied string).

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run2]
google_bigquery_routine.default is created in parallel with google_bigquery_table.default with no ordering between them. A routine whose definition_body references a table created by this module (e.g. a stored procedure doing INSERT/SELECT against a table from var.tables, or a UDF/TVF used by a table) can fail to create because the referenced base table may not exist yet. google_bigquery_table.views and google_bigquery_table.materialized_view already depends_on google_bigquery_table.default for exactly this reason; google_bigquery_routine.default should similarly depend on google_bigquery_table.default.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
google_bigquery_routine.default is created in parallel with google_bigquery_table.default. A SQL routine whose definition_body references a table created by this module can be submitted before that table exists, in which case BigQuery rejects the routine. The module already orders views and materialized views after base tables, but not routines.
